title.value: Adaptive patch foraging in deep reinforcement learning agents
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Adaptive patch foraging in deep reinforcement learning agents

extractions.description: The paper investigates deep reinforcement learning agents in an ecological patch foraging task. It demonstrates that machine learning agents can learn to patch forage adaptively, approaching optimal behavior and showing emergent internal dynamics similar to neural recordings from foraging non-human primates.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on AI research and modeling biological behavior, not directly on sustainable development, although it has implications for resource management.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This work suggests that agents interacting in complex environments with ecologically valid pressures arrive at common solutions, suggesting the emergence of foundational computations behind adaptive, intelligent behavior in both biological and artificial agents.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on AI and modeling biological systems, with no direct link to specific climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
primary_category.quote: Patch foraging is one of the most heavily studied behavioral optimization challenges in biology. However, despite its importance to biological intelligence, this behavioral optimization problem is understudied in artificial intelligence research.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any specific climate or ecological sub-category. It's about modeling a behavior.
primary_sub_category.quote: Here, we investigate deep reinforcement learning agents in an ecological patch foraging task.
